name: Silicone scar tape

lead: Silicone scar tape, or silicone gel sheeting, is a thin adhesive sheet worn over a healing or healed scar. It is used mainly for raised hypertrophic and keloid scars, and is sold over the counter for surgical and acne scars.

It is one of the more widely recommended topical scar treatments and is worn for many hours a day over months. Evidence quality is mixed: Cochrane reviews describe the trials as generally weak, although some data suggest benefit in scar-prone people.

paras: Silicone sheeting is thought to hydrate the stratum corneum and occlude the scar, which reduces fibroblast activity and collagen overproduction, and may also provide light pressure and temperature effects. The exact mechanism has not been established.

Side effects are mainly rashes, itching or maceration under the sheet, and it should not be applied over open wounds. The 2013 Cochrane review judged most trials to be of poor quality and could not clearly confirm benefit for prevention or treatment, so improvement may be modest and slow. It is not reported to remove a mature, flat scar.
